run_command.description: Run a command on the connected server, as you would type it at its prompt, and get back what it printed and its exit code. Use it to deploy, restart a service, check disk space, read a log, or run a script that lives on the server.

run_command.name: run_command

parameters.description: What to run on the server, exactly as you would type it at its prompt. It runs as the connected user, in that user's shell, so chain commands with && and quote values that contain spaces. Values from earlier steps can be put into it.
parameters.name: command

parameters.description: Run the command from this folder on the server, such as /var/www/app. Leave it empty to run from the user's home folder.
parameters.name: working_directory

parameters.description: Stop the command and fail the step if it has not finished within this many seconds. A command that waits for input never finishes, so give it none.
parameters.name: timeout

parameters.description: What to do when the command exits with a status other than 0. Continuing lets later steps read the exit code and the error output themselves, which suits a check whose failure is an answer rather than a problem.
parameters.name: on_error

exit_code.description: The command's exit status: 0 when it succeeded. -1 when it ended without reporting one, which usually means it was killed.

stderr.description: What the command printed to its error stream, without the line break it ended with. Many commands print progress and warnings here even when they succeed.

stdout.description: What the command printed, without the line break it ended with.

description: Run commands on your own servers over SSH and use what they print.
